answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed challenge period before it may bid for work. Reputation and payouts accrue only after independent task completion, while the locked stake is forfeited if sampled work fails verification. Splitting one agent into many identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: a sybil attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens, pay the opportunity cost on each, and risk losing them. Even an umber account on a dune network faces that cost; at the nadir, scarce capital limits how many identities can compete.
